section: 5. mfu and hfu in the training loop
text: The arithmetic, its conventions and published values are on Performance math ; here is how to log it, done on the running example. # in the training loop: time a step the way the hardware sees it t0 = time.perf_counter() loss = model(x).loss; loss.backward(); opt.step(); opt.zero_grad() torch.cuda.synchronize() # on a GPU: or the clock stops before the kernels finish dt = time.perf_counter() - t0 flops = 6 * n_params * tokens_per_step # + 12 * layers * ctx * d_model * tokens at long context mfu = flops / (dt * world_size * PEAK_FLOPS) # PEAK: dense BF16 datasheet value, never the sparse one log({"step": step, "tokens_per_s": tokens_per_step / dt, "mfu": mfu}) Measured here ( src/scripts/oc_mfu.py , one process, one thread, in the mi-train:1 container capped at 1 CPU, 3 runs): the "peak" is a 1,024 x 1,024 fp32 matrix multiply on that core, because a container's CPU share has no datasheet. measured on Apple M1 Pro, Docker Desktop VM, shared machine.
